author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Whatever I asked you have explained to me. I ask you once more, please tell me this: How do the attentive cross the flood of rebirth, old age, sorrow, and lamenting? Please, sage, answer me clearly, for truly you understand this matter."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I shall extol a teaching to you," replied the Buddha, "that is apparent in the present, not relying on legends. Having understood it, one who lives mindfully may cross over clinging in the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "And I rejoice, great seer, in that supreme teaching, having understood which, one who lives mindfully may cross over clinging in the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Once you've expelled relishing and dogmatism," replied the Buddha, "regarding everything you are aware of— above, below, all round, between— having cast aside consciousness, don't continue in existence.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: A mendicant who wanders meditating like this, diligent and mindful, calling nothing their own, would, being wise, give up the suffering of rebirth, old age, sorrow and lamenting right here."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I rejoice in the words of the great seer! You have expounded non-attachment well, Gotama. Clearly the Buddha has given up suffering, for truly you understand this matter.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Surely, sage, those you'd regularly instruct would also give up suffering. Having met, I bow especially to you, O spiritual giant; hopefully the Buddha may regularly instruct me."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Any brahmin recognized as a knowledge master, who has nothing, unattached to sensual life, clearly has crossed this flood, crossed to the far shore, kind, wishless.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: And a wise person here, a knowledge master, having untied the bond to life after life, free of craving, untroubled, with no need for hope, has crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this," said Venerable Dhotaka, "I long for your voice, great seer. After hearing your message, I shall train myself for extinguishment."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Well then, be keen, alert," replied the Buddha, "and mindful right here. After hearing this message, go on and train yourself for extinguishment."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I see in the world of gods and humans a brahmin traveling with nothing. I bow especially to you, All-seer: release me, Sakyan, from my indecisions."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I am not able to release anyone in the world who is indecisive, Dhotaka. But when you understand the best of teachings, you shall cross this flood."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Teach me, brahmin, out of compassion, the principle of seclusion so that I may understand. I wish to practice right here, peaceful, independent, unobstructed as space itself."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I shall extol that peace for you," replied the Buddha, "that is apparent in the present, not relying on legends. Having understood it, one who lives mindfully may cross over clinging in the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "And I rejoice, great seer, in that supreme peace, having understood which, one who lives mindfully may cross over clinging in the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Once you have understood that everything," replied the Buddha, "you are aware of in the world— above, below, all round, between— is a chain, don't crave for life after life."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Alone and independent, O Sakyan," said Venerable Upasīva, "I am not able to cross the great flood. Tell me a support, All-seer, depending on which I may cross this flood."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Mindfully contemplating nothingness," replied the Buddha, "depending on the perception 'there is nothing', cross the flood. Giving up sensual pleasures, refraining from chatter, watch day and night for the ending of craving."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "One who is free of desire for sensual pleasures," said Venerable Upasīva, "depending on nothingness, all else left behind, freed in the ultimate liberation of perception: might they remain there without traveling on?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "One free of desire for sensual pleasures," replied the Buddha, "depending on nothingness, all else left behind, freed in the ultimate liberation of perception: they might remain there without traveling on."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "If they were to remain there without traveling on, even for myriad years, All-seer, and, being freed, were to grow cool right there, would the consciousness of that sort pass away?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "As a flame tossed by a gust of wind," replied the Buddha, "comes to an end and cannot be reckoned; so too, a sage freed from the set of mental phenomena comes to an end and cannot be reckoned."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "One who has disappeared—do they not exist? Or are they free from disease for eternity? Please, sage, answer me clearly, for truly you understand this matter."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "One who has disappeared cannot be defined," replied the Buddha. "They have nothing by which others might describe them. When all things have been eradicated, eradicated, too, are all ways of speech."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "People say there are sages in the world," said Venerable Nanda, "but how is this the case? Is someone called a sage because of their knowledge, or because of their way of life?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Experts do not speak of a sage in terms of view, learning, or knowledge. Those who are sages live far from the crowd, I say, untroubled, with no need for hope."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "As to those ascetics and brahmins," said Venerable Nanda, "who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard, or in terms of precepts and vows, or in terms of countless different things. Living self-controlled in that matter, have they crossed over rebirth and old age, good fellow? I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "As to those ascetics and brahmins," replied the Buddha, "who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard, or in terms of precepts and vows, or in terms of countless different things. Even though they live self-controlled in that matter, they've not crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "As to those ascetics and brahmins," said Venerable Nanda, "who speak of purity in terms of what is seen or heard, or in terms of precepts and vows, or in terms of countless different things. You say they have not crossed the flood, sage. So who then in the world of gods and humans has crossed over rebirth and old age, good fellow? I ask you, Blessed One; please tell me this."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I don't say that all ascetics and brahmins," replied the Buddha, "are shrouded by rebirth and old age. There are those here who have given up all that is seen, heard, and thought, and precepts and vows, who have given up all the countless different things. Fully understanding craving, they are free of defilements, those people, I say, have crossed the flood."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I rejoice in the words of the great seer! You have expounded non-attachment well, Gotama. There are those here who have given up all that is seen, heard, and thought, and precepts and vows, who have given up all the countless different things. Fully understanding craving, they are free of defilements, those people, I agree, have crossed the flood."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Those who have previously answered me," said Venerable Hemaka, "before Gotama's teaching, said 'thus it was' or 'so it shall be'. All that was just the testament of hearsay; all that just fostered speculation: I found no delight in that.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: But you, sage, explain to me the teaching that destroys craving. Having understood it, one who lives mindfully may cross over clinging in the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "The removal of desire and lust, Hemaka, for pleasant things seen, heard, thought, or cognized here is extinguishment, the state that does not pass.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Those who have fully understood this, mindful, are quenched in this very life. Always at peace, they've crossed over clinging to the world."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "In whom sensual pleasures do not dwell," said Venerable Todeyya, "and for whom there is no craving, and who has crossed over indecision— of what kind is their liberation?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "In whom sensual pleasures do not dwell," replied the Buddha, "and for whom there is no craving, and who has crossed over indecision— there is no liberation that is further."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Are they free of hope, or are they still in need of hope? Do they possess wisdom, or are they still forming wisdom? O Sakyan, elucidate the sage to me, so that I may understand, All-seer."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "They are free of hope, they are not in need of hope. They possess wisdom, they are not still forming wisdom. That, Todeyya, is how to understand a sage, one who has nothing, unattached to sensual life."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "For those overwhelmed by old age and death," said Venerable Kappa, "stuck mid-stream as the terrifying flood arises, tell me an island, good fellow. Explain to me an island so this may occur no further."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "For those overwhelmed by old age and death," replied the Buddha, "stuck mid-stream as the terrifying flood arises, I shall tell you an island, Kappa.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Having nothing, taking nothing: this is the island with nothing further. I call it extinguishment, the ending of old age and death.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Those who have fully understood this, mindful, are quenched in this very life. They don't fall under Māra's sway, nor are they his footmen."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Hearing of the hero with no desire for sensual pleasures," said Venerable Jatukaṇṇī, "who has passed over the flood, I've come with a question for that desireless one. Tell me the state of peace, O natural visionary. Tell me this, Blessed One, as it really is.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: For, having mastered sensual desires, the Blessed One proceeds, as the blazing sun shines on the earth. May you of vast wisdom explain the teaching to me of little wisdom so that I may understand the giving up of rebirth and old age here."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "With desire for sensual pleasures dispelled," replied the Buddha, "seeing renunciation as sanctuary, don't be taking up or putting down anything at all.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: What came before, let wither away, and after, let there be nothing. If you don't grasp at the middle, you will live at peace.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: One rid of greed, brahmin, for the whole realm of name and form, has no defilements by which they might fall under the sway of Death."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I beseech you, the bastion-leaver, the craving-cutter, the imperturbable," said Venerable Bhadrāvudha, "the delight-leaver, the flood-crosser, the freed, the formulation-leaver, the intelligent. Different people have gathered from across the nations

author: Gotama Buddha
text: wishing to hear your word, O hero. After hearing the spiritual giant they will depart from here. Please, sage, answer them clearly, for truly you understand this matter."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Dispel all craving for attachments," replied the Buddha, "above, below, all round, between. For whatever a personage grasps in the world, Māra pursues them right there.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: So let a mindful mendicant who understands not grasp anything in all the world, observing that, in clinging to attachments, these people cling to the domain of death."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "To the meditator, rid of hopes," said Venerable Udaya, "who has completed the task, is free of defilements, and has gone beyond all things, I have come seeking with a question. Tell me the liberation by enlightenment, the smashing of ignorance."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "The giving up of both" replied the Buddha, "sensual desires and displeasures; the casting aside of dullness, and the prevention of remorse;

author: Gotama Buddha
text: pure equanimity and mindfulness, preceded by investigation of principles— this, I declare, is liberation by enlightenment, the smashing of ignorance."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "What fetters the world? How does it travel about? With the giving up of what is extinguishment spoken of?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Delight fetters the world. It travels about by means of thought. With the giving up of craving extinguishment is spoken of."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "For one living mindfully, how does consciousness cease? We've come to ask the worthy sir: let us hear what you say."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Not taking pleasure in feeling internally and externally— for one living mindfully, that's how consciousness ceases."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "To the one who reveals the past," said Venerable Posāla, "who is imperturbable, with doubts cut off, and who has gone beyond all things, I have come seeking with a question.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Consider one who perceives that form has vanished, who has entirely given up the body, and who sees nothing at all internally and externally. I ask the Sakyan about knowledge for them; how should that sort be guided?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "The Realized One directly knows," said the Buddha, "all planes of consciousness. And he knows this one who remains, committed to that as their final goal.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Understanding that desire for rebirth in the dimension of nothingness is a fetter, and directly knowing what this really means, one then discerns that matter clearly. That is their knowledge of truth, the brahmin who has lived the life."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Twice I have asked the Sakyan," said Venerable Mogharāja, "but you haven't answered me, O Clear-eyed One. I have heard that the divine seer answers when questioned a third time.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: Regarding this world, the other world, and the realm of divinity with its gods, I'm not familiar with the view of the renowned Gotama.

author: Gotama Buddha
text: So I have come seeking with a question for the one of excellent vision. How to look upon the world so the King of Death won't see you?"

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Look upon the world as empty, Mogharāja, ever mindful. Having uprooted the theory of self, you may thus cross over death. That's how to look upon the world so the King of Death won't see you."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "I am old, feeble, and pallid," said Venerable Piṅgiya, "my eyes unclear, my hearing faint— don't let me perish while still confused. Explain the teaching so that I may understand the giving up of rebirth and old age here."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Seeing them being harmed on account of forms," replied the Buddha, "those negligent folk are inflicted on account of forms— therefore, Piṅgiya, being diligent, give up form so as not to be reborn."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "The four quarters, the intermediate directions, below, and above: in these ten directions there's nothing at all in the world that you've not seen, heard, thought, or cognized. Explain the teaching so that I may understand the giving up of rebirth and old age here."

author: Gotama Buddha
text: "Observing mankind sunk in craving," replied the Buddha, "tormented, mired in old age; therefore, Piṅgiya, being diligent, give up craving so as not to be reborn."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: This was said by the Buddha while staying in the land of the Magadhans at the Pāsāṇaka Shrine. When requested by the sixteen brahmin devotees, he answered their questions one by one. If you understand the meaning and the teaching of each of these questions, and practice in line with the teaching, you may go right to the far shore of old age and death. These teachings are said to lead to the far shore, which is why the name of this exposition of the teaching is "The Way to the Far Shore".

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: Ajita, Tissametteyya, Puṇṇaka and Mettagū, Dhotaka and Upasiva, Nanda and then Hemaka,

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: both Todeyya and Kappa, and Jatukaṇṇī the astute, Bhadrāvudha and Udaya, and the brahmin Posāla, Mogharāja the intelligent, and Piṅgiya the great seer:

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: they approached the Buddha, the seer of consummate conduct. Asking their subtle questions, they came to the most excellent Buddha.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: The Buddha answered their questions in accordance with truth. The sage satisfied the brahmins with his answers to their questions.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: Those who were satisfied by the Clear-eyed One, the Buddha, Kinsman of the Sun, led the spiritual life in his presence, the one of such outstanding wisdom.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: If you practice in accordance with each of these questions as taught by the Buddha, you'll go from the near shore to the far.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.18 Homage to the Way to the Far Shore
text: Developing the supreme path, you'll go from the near shore to the far. This path is for going to the far shore; that's why it's called "The Way to the Far Shore".

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: "I shall keep reciting the Way to the Far Shore," said Venerable Piṅgiya, "which was taught as it was seen by the immaculate one of vast intelligence. He is desireless, unentangled, a spiritual giant: why would he speak falsely?

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Come, let me extol in sweet words of praise the one who's given up stains and delusions, conceit and contempt.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: The Buddha, All-seer, dispeller of darkness, has gone to world's end, beyond all rebirths; he is free of defilements, and has given up all suffering, the rightly-named one, brahmin, is revered by me.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Like a bird that flees a little copse, to roost in a forest abounding in fruit, I've left the near-sighted behind, like a swan come to a great river.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Those who explained to me previously, before Gotama's teaching, said 'thus it was' or 'so it shall be'. All that was just the testament of hearsay; all that just fostered speculation.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Alone, the dispeller of darkness is brilliant, a beacon: Gotama, vast in wisdom, Gotama, vast in intelligence.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: He is the one who taught me Dhamma, apparent in the present life, immediately effective, the untroubled, the end of craving, to which there is no compare."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: "Why would you dwell apart from him even for an hour, Piṅgiya? From Gotama, vast in wisdom, from Gotama, vast in intelligence?

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: He is the one who taught you Dhamma, apparent in the present life, immediately effective, the untroubled, the end of craving, to which there is no compare."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: "I never dwell apart from him, not even for an hour, brahmin. From Gotama, vast in wisdom, from Gotama, vast in intelligence.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: He is the one who taught me Dhamma, apparent in the present life, immediately effective, the untroubled, the end of craving, to which there is no compare.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Being diligent, I see him in my mind's eye day and night. I spend the night in homage to him, hence I think I dwell with him.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: My faith and joy and intent and mindfulness never stray from Gotama's teaching. I bow to whatever direction the one of vast wisdom heads.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: I'm old and feeble, so my body cannot go there, but I always travel in my thoughts, for my mind, brahmin, is bound to him.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Lying floundering in the mud, I drifted from island to island. Then I saw the Buddha, the undefiled one who has crossed the flood."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: "Just as Vakkali was committed to faith— Bhadrāvudha and Gotama of Āḷavī too— so too you should commit to faith. You will go, Piṅgiya, beyond the domain of death."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: "My confidence grows as I hear the word of the sage, the Buddha with veil cast off, so kind and eloquent.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: Having directly known all about the gods, he understands all top to bottom, the Teacher who settles all questions for those who admit their doubts.

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: The unfaltering, the unshakable: that to which there is no compare. For sure I will go there, I have no doubt of that. Remember me as one whose mind is made up."

author: Gotama Buddha
division_title: 5.19 Preserving the Way to the Far Shore
text: The Anthology of Discourses is completed.
